summary.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
summary.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

financial_highlights.metric: Return on average AUM / average tangible equity

segments.name: MSME loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR 8,873 crore, 79% of book, with Q4 disbursements of INR 785 crore. Average ticket size remains below INR 2.5 lakh and LTV is about 56-57%.

segments.name: Loan against gold
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,374 crore, 21% of book, growing 63% YoY; management says growth is mainly price-driven and the share may move toward 25%. Around 220 of 251 branches are pure gold branches.

segments.name: Co-origination (with ICICI)
segments.commentary: Co-origination was 16% of Q4 disbursements and 18-19% of AUM, and is expected to hold similar levels through FY27.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance unchanged at 5-7% per quarter; management says the segment could double the book in 3-3.5 years.
Spreads expected to hold at around 9% current level; over 90% of the book is variable-rate.
Opex expected to fall 20-25 bps through FY27 as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected to stay range-bound around 1.38%, with possible benefit of about 5 bps.
Branch network to stabilise at about 275 (from 251) during the year; 46 branches were added in FY26 against 25 guided.
Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected at 75:25; co-origination at 18-19% of AUM.
Capital: at 33% CRAR, growth could run about 2 years before needing fresh capital, with CRAR falling to about 24-26%.
capex_capacity: Branches: 251 at March 2026 after adding 21 in Q4 and 46 in FY26; target to stabilise at about 275 in FY27.
Branch expansion is gated by state profitability; new states are run slowly for 18-24 months before scaling, with about 60% of branches older than 3 years.
Currently present in about one-fourth of districts in operating states (about 30% per Aseem Dhru) across 15 states.
Management says it will not add DSAs or connectors for at least two years; direct model retained.
Leverage at 1.9x debt/equity; management says capital is sufficient for roughly two years of growth.
demand_pricing: Management said growth in gold has been mostly price-driven rather than tonnage-driven; gold prices are expected to stay range-bound or flat.
Disbursements have been soft YoY; management said it paused momentum in some South, East and West pockets, and could return to around INR 300 crore per month when conditions improve.
South disbursals and AUM grew more slowly last year, which lifted the West's share of AUM (management said mix to stay similar for two quarters).
Early April data showed no new stress in sectors hit by LPG and fertilizer pressures; bounce rates marginally lower.
Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27; G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee and branch opex per unit flat for many quarters, and how long can that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

risks_watch: Macro shocks: oil price pass-through, weaker rupee, poor monsoon/El Nino, Gulf remittance risk, all flagged by management.
Gold price reversal would slow the gold book, which is 21% of AUM and the main driver of growth.
Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).
Disbursement volumes are down YoY and branches added in gold and MSME may not reach productivity targets as planned.
Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and capital, but cautious on the macro: management repeatedly stressed that guidance is unchanged and credit cost is held conservatively. Evasive on rating upgrade timing and on the West AUM share jump, which was deferred offline.
key_quotes: Our overall guidance remains unchanged at 5% to 7% on a quarterly basis.
Lending is a commodity business, and we are all price takers, not price setters.
Costs are taken, benefits to accrue.

adds.what: Branches: 251 at March 2026 (21 added in Q4, 46 in FY26) heading to ~275 during FY27

growth.why: Guides AUM growth of 5-7% per quarter (about 22-31% annualised) unchanged, backed by 251 branches expanding to ~275 and co-origination, but disbursements are soft and gold growth is mainly price-driven, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spreads at 9.09% (+56 bps YoY, +5 bps QoQ) with cost of borrowing down 83 bps to 8.52%, but management guides spreads flat at ~9% and says over 90% of the book is variable-rate, so further expansion is limited; opex falling 20-25 bps through FY27 is the main operating lever.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches at 251 after 46 added in FY26 against 25 guided, with management targeting ~275 in FY27 (about 9.6% more branches), though new states take 18-24 months to scale and expansion is gated by state profitability.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter (about 22-31% annualised) with AUM at INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY, and management says current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year; soft disbursements (about INR 300 crore per month target when conditions improve) temper this.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex discussed; CRAR at 32.8% and leverage 1.9x debt/equity give about two years of growth before fresh capital is needed, and the direct model with no DSAs or connectors is retained for at least two years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept AUM growth at 5-7% per quarter, spreads flat at ~9%, and credit cost range-bound at ~1.38%, and called its credit cost guidance conservative only in the sense of a possible ~5 bps benefit.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Disbursements are soft YoY, pockets in South, East and West have paused, stage 2 has risen from about 6% to 16% while credit cost is held at 1.38%, and gold growth is price-driven with gold prices expected flat or range-bound.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed.

rows.label: Cost of borrowing flat in FY27
rows.why: Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27 with over 90% of the book variable-rate, though G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged; cost of borrowing already fell 83 bps YoY to 8.52%.

rows.label: Opex to AUM down 20-25 bps through FY27
rows.why: Opex at 3.93% of AUM (down 69 bps YoY, flat QoQ) with upfront state, regional and supervisor investment already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost.

rows.label: Rating upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give timing and did not guide it; a rating upgrade is possible but not guided, with CRAR at 32.8% and GNPA at 2.61%.
